Rust 2.0 ships

By Ann Example, October 16, 2026

The Rust project released version 2.0 today, the first major version since 1.0 shipped more than a decade ago. The release focuses on making async code easier to write and on a faster compiler.

The headline change is a reworked borrow checker that accepts more correct programs without annotations, which the team says removes most of the friction new users report in surveys.

What changes for existing code

Existing crates keep compiling: editions still let each crate opt in to new syntax on its own schedule, and the migration tool rewrites the few patterns that changed meaning.

  • Async closures are stable.
  • Incremental builds are about 30% faster.
